- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >50% above recent mean), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 15–30% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is high, model is prone to overconfidence; cap forecasts at 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates during high sentiment + low price history; adjust upward by 5–15% if sentiment >0.67 and price <2.20.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 18-day mean is >2.25, forecast should not exceed 2.50 unless sentiment >0.80.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
